# S15 — Daemon snapshot cache and per-part refresh

An in-memory snapshot cache in the daemon that every client reads, with a
refresh schedule per part and pushed change notices (`dash.cache`,
`dash.refresh`, `boundary.git-head`).

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-10-19** — Review FAIL: M1 finish() after Forget and re-add corrupts the new entry (dedup broken, old path value served); fix round with L1, L3, L5 and a test for the pending path.

trust: unverified; by: Jon R

**Not in this slice:** cache files on disk, file watching, reading `.slicer/` or `decisions/`, and adopting `slicer snapshot` (later).

## Why

Measured under load, one slicer call costs 0.4-1.4 s and about 0.6 s CPU;
S03 as built re-runs every call per request, about 7 s CPU per
`ork status` over four projects (docs/review-2026-10-19-integration.md,
R1-R3).

## Files

- `internal/cache/` (new), `internal/daemon/` (serve from the cache, push
  notices), `internal/ipc/` (a subscribe method), `internal/source/` only if
  needed.

## Failing tests

- Two clients asking at once cause one CLI call per part, not two.
- At most 4 CLI processes run at once across projects.
- Items and runs refresh every 5 s for the visible project and 30 s for
  the others; goals and decided records every 5 min, on a git HEAD change
  (`git rev-parse HEAD` only), on tab open and on an explicit refresh.
- A failed refresh keeps the last good value, marks it stale with the
  error code and age, and retries once on `corrupt`, `locked` or a timeout.
- A subscribed client gets a notice when a part's value changes, and none
  when it is unchanged.
- With a fake clock and fake CLIs; no real slicer, adj or git.

## Implement

- The visible project comes from the clients' subscriptions.
- Values carry the time they were read and the error, if any.
